note: The merged capability set for CrowdDeck, assembled from the researched feature sets. 'from' records which analysed product established the expectation. Priorities are proposals for SPECIFICATION.md review, not commitments.

domains.name: A. Performance Engine
domains.summary: The real-time audio core. Everything here has a hard latency budget and must run out of the browser.

capabilities.name: 4 independent decks with per-deck EQ, filter, gain and crossfader assignment
capabilities.note: Four decks is the table stakes established by every analysed product.

capabilities.name: Beatgrid detection and manual grid editing
capabilities.note: Everything downstream - sync, loops, quantize, auto-transitions, lighting cues - depends on grid accuracy.

capabilities.name: Musical key detection and key-lock / pitch-independent tempo
capabilities.note: Key-lock quality is a licence decision: SoundTouch (LGPL) vs Rubber Band (GPL/commercial).

capabilities.name: Sync lock with explicit leader deck, plus manual tempo
capabilities.note: The leader deck also becomes the master tempo source published to MIDI clock and Ableton Link.

capabilities.name: Hot cues, memory cues, loops, beat jump, slicer, quantize, slip mode
Per-stem control on every deck (vocals / harmonics / drums / bass)
capabilities.note: Precompute stems on ingest and cache them. Live separation is not achievable at Demucs quality.

capabilities.name: Chainable per-deck FX with an XY performance pad
Sampler and step-sequencing pattern player
capabilities.note: The natural bridge to the MIDI instrument domain - the pattern player is what an external drum machine syncs against.

capabilities.name: DVS timecode vinyl / CD control
Sandbox / practice mode - audition and build the next transition without touching the room output
capabilities.note: Unusually important here: the DJ needs to pre-fly patron requests before they hit the room.

capabilities.name: Microphone and aux inputs with ducking, plus recording and Icecast broadcast

domains.name: B. Venue & Crowd Plane
domains.summary: The TouchTunes half. This is where the differentiation lives - no open-source project covers this properly today.

capabilities.name: Patron joins a venue by QR code or short URL, no app install required
capabilities.note: QR beats a map-based venue finder for a self-hosted product - the patron is already in the room.

capabilities.name: Live queue with each patron's exact position in line
capabilities.note: TouchTunes' single most-cited feature. Visible position is what makes waiting tolerable.

capabilities.name: Paid priority - jump the queue (Fast Pass / Song Upgrade equivalent)
capabilities.note: The core monetisation primitive. Must be pluggable, and disable-able for free/private events.

capabilities.name: Credit wallet with non-expiring balance and auto-refill
capabilities.note: Payment provider must be an adapter; many self-hosted deployments will run creditless.

capabilities.name: Democratic voting to reorder the queue, with vote decay and cooldown
capabilities.note: Voting and paid priority are two orderings of the same queue - the scheduler must support blending them.

capabilities.name: Fair-queue anti-monopoly rules: per-patron limits, artist/track cooldown, rate limiting
capabilities.note: Without this one patron plays the same song six times and the venue turns the system off.

capabilities.name: Venue policy engine: explicit-content filter, genre/artist allow and block lists, dayparting, volume schedule
capabilities.note: The venue owner must always be able to override the crowd.

capabilities.name: Staff override console - skip, veto, refund, mute, lock the queue, panic-stop
Never-silent fallback rotation when the request queue empties
capabilities.note: The system must degrade into a well-behaved background-music player, automatically.

capabilities.name: Loyalty points, emoji reactions and now-playing social feed
Multi-venue / multi-tenant operator console with remote scheduling and reporting
capabilities.note: The operator route model is how this class of product actually makes money.

capabilities.name: Venue display screen - now playing, up next, QR to join, visualiser

domains.name: C. Fusion Layer (the actual novelty)
domains.summary: Where the DJ plane and the crowd plane meet. No analysed product, open or closed, does this.

capabilities.name: Crowd requests land in the DJ's staging lane, not directly on the output
capabilities.note: The DJ approves, reorders and beatmatches requests. This is the single design decision that makes a jukebox and a DJ rig coexist.

capabilities.name: Autonomous mode - engine auto-mixes the crowd queue with beatmatched transitions when no DJ is present
capabilities.note: A venue runs unattended most of the day and staffed at night. One system, two modes.

capabilities.name: Handoff: DJ takes or releases control mid-set without a gap in audio
Request-aware transition planning using intro/outro and phrase detection
Crowd signal surfaced to the DJ: request heatmap, vote velocity, unfilled genre demand
capabilities.note: Turning the request stream into live audience telemetry is a genuinely new capability.

capabilities.name: Patrons can only request what is playable and licensed in that venue's catalog
capabilities.note: Search is scoped by the venue policy engine, so an unplayable request is never offered.

domains.name: D. MIDI & Systems Interconnection
domains.summary: The interconnect fabric. Explicitly a first-class subsystem, not a settings page.

capabilities.name: MIDI 1.0 and MIDI 2.0 / UMP I/O with hot-plug and stable port identity
capabilities.note: Windows 11 MIDI Services, macOS CoreMIDI (since 2021) and ALSA (kernel 6.5+) all now carry UMP natively. Mappings must bind to stable handles, not port indices.

capabilities.name: MIDI learn with soft-takeover / pickup, plus visual mapped-state indication
capabilities.note: Soft-takeover prevents parameter jumps when a physical knob is out of sync with software state.

capabilities.name: Declarative, shareable, forkable controller mapping format
capabilities.note: Mixxx's XML-plus-JavaScript model with typed API declarations is the best open prior art. Ship a controller wizard.

capabilities.name: HID controller support for high-resolution jog wheels
capabilities.note: 7-bit MIDI gives only 128 steps per rotation; HID is required for credible scratch feel.

capabilities.name: MIDI clock out/in at 24 PPQN, with the leader deck as tempo source
capabilities.note: Clock is the tempo-accurate sync path; MTC is positional reference only and too coarse for beat-accurate triggering.

capabilities.name: Ableton Link peer sync for tempo, beat, phase and start/stop
capabilities.note: How phones, laptops and hardware in the room join the same timeline with no cables. Watch the GPL/commercial licence split.

capabilities.name: External MIDI instrument integration - keyboards, drum machines, grooveboxes play in time with the deck
capabilities.note: The explicit brief: MIDI as an instrument interface, not only a control surface. Instruments become an additional content source, alongside files.

capabilities.name: OSC in/out for tablets, VJ software and show-control systems
Mackie Control / HUI emulation so studio control surfaces work as mixers
capabilities.note: Opens up a large installed base of motorised-fader surfaces beyond DJ-specific hardware.

capabilities.name: Web MIDI path for browser-based mapping and lightweight control
capabilities.note: Convenience only. Safari has no Web MIDI support on macOS or iOS, and Chrome 124+ requires a permission prompt over HTTPS - so the native path stays authoritative.

domains.name: E. Content & Catalog
domains.summary: Where the music comes from. Deliberately pluggable, because licensing differs per deployment.

capabilities.name: Local library ingest with fingerprint-backed tagging and de-duplication
Self-hosted server sources over the OpenSubsonic API
capabilities.note: Also expose our own OpenSubsonic endpoint so existing clients work against CrowdDeck immediately.

capabilities.name: Creative Commons catalog providers
capabilities.note: The licence-clean default catalog, so a fresh install has legal music in it on first run.

capabilities.name: Pluggable licensed-streaming adapters behind a provider interface
capabilities.note: Every one of these needs a commercial agreement; ship the interface, not unauthorised implementations.

capabilities.name: Live MIDI instruments and external inputs registered as first-class queueable sources
capabilities.note: A keyboard or drum machine appears in the queue like a track does - the interconnection idea taken to its conclusion.

capabilities.name: Precomputed analysis cache: beatgrid, key, loudness, phrases, stems, waveform
capabilities.note: One ingest pass feeds decks, auto-mix, lighting and patron preview alike.

capabilities.name: ReplayGain / EBU R128 loudness normalisation across mixed sources
capabilities.note: Non-negotiable when a CC track, a local file and a live instrument follow one another.

capabilities.name: Karaoke media support (CDG / MP4+lyrics) with singer rotation

domains.name: F. Show Control
domains.summary: Making the room respond to the music.

capabilities.name: Beat- and phrase-synced DMX512 / Art-Net / sACN lighting
capabilities.note: rekordbox's phrase-aware auto-lighting is the benchmark; OLA plus the QLC+ fixture library gets us most of the way.

capabilities.name: Synchronised multi-zone audio across rooms
capabilities.note: Patio, main room and restrooms are different zones with different policies and volumes.

capabilities.name: Video / visualiser output on the venue screen
Digital signage and venue promo slots between tracks
capabilities.note: A real revenue lever for operators.

domains.name: G. Platform & Operations
domains.summary: What makes it deployable in a real venue rather than a demo.

capabilities.name: Offline-first venue runtime - full function with no internet
from: TouchTunes cloud dependency is a weakness
capabilities.note: A cloud-dependent jukebox goes silent when the venue's DSL drops. Local-first is a genuine advantage over TouchTunes.

capabilities.name: Headless server plus separate operator, DJ and patron clients
Open, documented HTTP + WebSocket API for the whole system
capabilities.note: Third-party clients are how an open project out-features a closed one.

capabilities.name: Single-command deploy (container / compose) with a sane default catalog
Venue analytics: plays, requests, revenue, peak hours, unfilled demand
No telemetry by default; all data stays in the venue

domains.name: H. Licensing, Compliance & Governance
domains.summary: The part hobby projects skip and venues get fined for.

capabilities.name: Per-venue licensing profile recording which PRO licences are held
capabilities.note: The Jukebox License Office shut down in 2025, so operators now need separate ASCAP, BMI and SESAC licences. Software should track this, not assume it.

capabilities.name: Catalog sources tagged with their licence class and public-performance status
capabilities.note: The system must be able to answer 'may this venue legally play this track right now'.

capabilities.name: Reporting export of what was actually performed
capabilities.note: Play logs are the evidence trail for PRO reporting and label statements.

capabilities.name: Hard refusal to source venue catalog from consumer accounts or downloaders
capabilities.note: Consumer streaming subscriptions do not grant public-performance rights. Designing this out is a feature.

capabilities.name: Clean licence separation between the permissive core and any GPL-derived planes
capabilities.note: Decided before the first line of engine code, because it is nearly impossible to unwind later.
